title: GPU VulnDB entry
description: One vulnerability, or one design-level weakness, affecting the stack that GPU infrastructure runs on.

id.description: Stable key and filename. A CVE id where one exists, otherwise NCVD-<year>-<seq>-<slug>.

cve.description: Null for design-level weaknesses that have no CVE and never will.

aliases.description: Named-vulnerability branding only, e.g. NVIDIAScape. Not component qualifiers.

layer.description: Which layer of the stack the flaw lives in.

kev.description: Listed in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

impact.description: What an attacker gets. Written for an operator, not copied from the CVE record.

attack_vector.description: Who has to be able to reach what, for this to be exploitable.

remediation.description: What the operator has to actually do. This is the field that makes the entry worth more than an NVD lookup.

fleet.description: Blast radius across a fleet: how many nodes carry it, and what remediation costs.

pain_class.description: What remediation actually costs, ordered roughly cheapest to most disruptive.

status.description: Quality tier. 'curated' is bulk-imported from vendor advisories with machine assistance and is not individually human-verified. 'reviewed' means a maintainer confirmed every field against primary sources. 'stub' is a placeholder with references but no analysis.

contributor.description: GitHub profile of whoever wrote or last verified this entry. Distinct from the researcher who found the flaw.

discovered_by.description: Credit for the original research. A list, because findings usually have more than one author.

published_at.description: ISO 8601. Deliberately not the YYYY/MM/DD strings other databases use.

known_exploited.description: Exploited in the wild, independent of whether CISA has listed it.

then.description: A CVE-keyed entry must carry the matching cve field.

else.description: Anything with a severity bucket must carry the score it was derived from.
